title: Constructible module sheaves generate the category
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring. Every sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ (an object of $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]) is a quotient of a coproduct of constructible sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]: there are a set $I$, constructible sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules $C_i$ ($i\in I$) whose coproduct $\bigoplus_{i\in I}C_i$ exists in $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and an epimorphism $\bigoplus_{i\in I}C_i\to F$ of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules.

proof.text:
*A separating family of extensions by zero.* Write $\Mod=\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)=\Mod(\Lambda_X)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-essentially-small-cover] choose a set $\mathcal S$ of objects $U	o X$ of $X_{\Et}$ with $U$ affine such that every object of $X_{\Et}$ has a covering by members of $\mathcal S$; for $U\in\mathcal S$ let $j_{U!}\Lambda_U$ be the sheafification of the presheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules $V\mapsto igoplus_{\varphi\in\mathrm{Mor}(V,U)}\Lambda_X(V)$, as in [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] (2) all small coproducts exist in $\Mod$, in particular $G= igoplus_{U\in\mathcal S}j_{U!}\Lambda_U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian] (statement and the fifth step of its proof, 'A generator') $G$ is a separator of $\Mod$: for $u
eq v:M	o N$ there is $h:G	o M$ with $uh
eq vh$. (If one reads only the statement's 'generator' in the subobject sense: for $u
eq v$ put $w=u-v
eq0$; then $\ker w\subsetneq M$ is a proper subobject, so some $h:G	o M$ does not factor through $\ker w$, i.e. $wh
eq0$, i.e. $uh
eq vh$.)

source.place: Lemma 093B (2) (B = a set of affine objects of X_et satisfying Situation 093A (1)), proof via Lemma 03EW (3); the Hom identification Hom(j_{U!}O_U, F) = F(U) is equation 0G1V (equation-map-lower-shriek-OU-into-module)

proof.text: *The epimorphism.* Let $F\in\Mod$. Let $I_F$ be the set of pairs $(Y,h)$ with $Y=j_{U!}\Lambda_U$ for some $U\in\mathcal S$ and $h:Y\to F$ a morphism of $\Mod$; it is a set since $\mathcal S$ is a set and Hom-sets of $\Mod$ are sets. The coproduct $\bigoplus_{(Y,h)\in I_F}Y$ exists by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] (2). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-separating-family-epi-coproduct] to $\mathcal C=\Mod$, the family $(j_{U!}\Lambda_U)_{U\in\mathcal S}$ (whose coproduct $G$ is a separator by step 1) and $A=F$: the morphism $\pi:\bigoplus_{(Y,h)\in I_F}Y\to F$ equal to $h$ on the summand $(Y,h)$ is an epimorphism. (Under $\mathrm{Hom}(j_{U!}\Lambda_U,F)\cong F(U)$ the index pairs are the pairs $(U,s)$, $s\in F(U)$, of Stacks 03EW, and $\pi$ is the sum of the maps attached to the sections $s$.)

*Each summand is constructible.* Let $(Y,h)\in I_F$, $Y=j_{U!}\Lambda_U$ with $U\in\mathcal S$. The structure map $U\to X$ is etale (an object of $X_{\Et}$), $U$ is affine, hence quasi-compact (the spectrum of a ring is quasi-compact) and quasi-separated (the diagonal of an affine scheme over $\mathbf Z$ is a closed immersion, hence quasi-compact) [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and $\Lambda$ is a finite $\Lambda$-module. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-free-sheaf-constructible] with $M=\Lambda$ (whose sheaf $j_!\underline\Lambda_U$ is by its definition the sheafification of the same presheaf $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{\varphi}\Lambda_X(V)$, i.e. $Y$), $Y$ is a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules.

source.place: Lemma 03SA (lemma-torsion-colimit-constructible), proof of (3) (line 12249: 'By Lemmas 03S8 and 03RZ these cokernels are constructible'), using Lemma 03S8 (3) with U quasi-compact and quasi-separated

proof.text: *Conclusion.* Take $I=I_F$ and $C_{(Y,h)}=Y$: by step 3 every $C_i$ is constructible, and by step 2 $\pi:\bigoplus_{i\in I}C_i\to F$ is an epimorphism, so $F$ is a quotient of a coproduct of constructible sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules (in the abelian category $\Mod$, $F\cong\mathrm{Coker}(\ker\pi\to\bigoplus_iC_i)$).
